newsitem.title: UK: UK Internet seen winning bigger share of adverts.
newsitem.headline: UK Internet seen winning bigger share of adverts.

text.p: Companies in Britain spent an estimated four million stg ($6.4 million) on advertising on the Internet in 1996, NewMediaAge magazine reported on Friday.

The weekly magazine quoted a report by investment house Dresdner Kleinwort Benson (DKB) that predicted Internet advertising's share of total advertising could rise to two percent by 2000 from a current 0.4 percent.
The report, called "Going Digital", forecast the value of UK advertising on the Internet would reach 266 million stg by 2001.

The figures were was based on the expected number of Internet subscribers in Britain reaching 4.25 million by 2001 and on an 11-fold increase in the level of advertising expenditure per UK Internet user.

The magazine quoted DKB's Michael Hilton, who wrote the report, as saying the four million stg figure for 1996 was calculated by scaling down estimates of the global Internet advertising market in line with UK "traffic levels".

Hilton said the two percent forecast for 2001 was in contrast to a prediction by Jupiter Communications that ads placed on the Internet by companies in the United States would amount to four to six percent of the total U.S. advertising market by 2001.
Jupiter is a New York-based research, consulting and publishing company that specialises in consumer online and interactive technologies.

The DKB report said it was unlikely the UK market for Internet advertising would grow faster than forecast, but Hilton said there was a lack of relevant statistics on Internet advertising in Britain. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds Sterling)
